cases.exposure_context_quote: A 40-year-old Nepali male presented with alleged history of suicidal ingestion of 30 ml of Amitraz (12.5% W/V) following a dispute with his wife under influence of alcohol was presented to emergency room of Lumbini Provincial Hospital, Rupandehi, Nepal after 1 hour of ingestion.
cases.agent_quote: suicidal ingestion of 30 ml of Amitraz (12.5% W/V) ... This patient ingested approximately 3750 mg orally (46.8 mg/kg).
cases.circumstance: Suicidal ingestion following a dispute with his wife, under the influence of alcohol.

symptoms.finding: three episodes of non-projectile vomiting and epigastric pain
symptoms.quote: He had three episodes of non-projectile vomiting and pain in the epigastric region.

symptoms.finding: hypotension (BP 100/70 mmHg) and bradycardia (radial pulse 52 bpm)
symptoms.quote: His Blood pressure was 100/70 mmHg in right brachial artery, radial pulse was 52 beats per minute, SpO2 was 96% in room air, respiratory rate was 15 breaths/minutes, temperature 97°F and GRBS 119 mg/dL.

symptoms.finding: bilateral pinpoint pupils, sluggish to light
symptoms.quote: On examination, his both pupils were pin-point and sluggish to reaction to light.
Twelve leads electrocardiograph (ECG) showed sinus bradycardia (Fig. 1).

symptoms.finding: decreased consciousness (GCS E1V2M3) with respiratory depression (RR 9/min) 40–60 min after presentation
symptoms.quote: After 40–60 minutes of emergency presentation his Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) dropped to E1V2M3 with respiratory rate of 9 breaths/minute.

labs.name: ECG
labs.value: sinus bradycardia, then sinus tachycardia post-atropine challenge
labs.quote: Twelve leads electrocardiograph (ECG) showed sinus bradycardia (Fig. 1). ... His 12 leads ECG showed sinus tachycardia (Fig. 2) post-atropine challenge test.

labs.name: arterial blood gas
labs.quote: His arterial blood gas (ABG) was normal.

labs.name: blood parameters incl. thyroid function test and ABG (day 3)
labs.quote: he was extubated as he was hemodynamically stable, and his blood parameters were normal including thyroid function test (TFT) and ABG.

treatment.name: gastric lavage with normal saline and activated charcoal (1 g/kg), within 30 min of presentation
treatment.quote: Gastric lavage was done within 30 minutes of presentation to emergency with normal saline and activated charcoal (1 g/kg), and patient was given 500 mL of 0.9% normal saline and 1.2 mg of atropine intravenously.

treatment.name: atropine 1.2 mg IV (atropine challenge test)
treatment.quote: patient was given 500 mL of 0.9% normal saline and 1.2 mg of atropine intravenously. This resulted in an increased heart rate to 114 bpm indicating atropine challenge test to be positive.

treatment.name: intubation under IV ketamine and midazolam; ICU mechanical ventilation
treatment.quote: He was then intubated in the emergency room under proper sedation with intravenous ketamine and midazolam. Patient was then shifted to intensive care unit (ICU) for mechanical ventilation.

treatment.name: symptomatic treatment: IV fluids, prophylactic antibiotics, sedation with IV midazolam and fentanyl
treatment.quote: As there is no known antidote for amitraz, only symptomatic treatment was done, which includes intravenous fluids, prophylactic antibiotics, sedation by intravenous midazolam and fentanyl.

treatment.name: extubation day 3; psychiatric consultation; sertraline prescribed
treatment.quote: On the third day he was extubated ... He was prescribed Sertraline and advised to follow-up in 2 weeks.

cases.icu_admission: yes (shifted to ICU for mechanical ventilation; extubated day 3, medical ward day 4)
cases.outcome: survived; discharged on day 5 after psychiatric consultation; at 2-week follow-up basic blood investigations normal and treated per depression guidelines
cases.outcome_quote: On the fourth day, he was shifted to medical ward and on fifth day he was discharged from ward after psychiatric consultation. He was prescribed Sertraline and advised to follow-up in 2 weeks. After 2 weeks he came back for follow-up in the medical and psychiatric outpatient department. His basic blood investigations came normal and was treated accordingly based on depression guidelines.
cases.sequelae: none — no neurological deficit and no cardiovascular symptoms at extubation
cases.notes: Authors note amitraz poisoning can be misdiagnosed as organophosphate/carbamate poisoning; atropine challenge test positive argued against OP poisoning.
